title: Routing rule safety harness: modular validator for region, tier and fallback semantics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Replace the ad-hoc routing rule checks with a modular validation harness that enforces correct semantics for region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants. The validator must operate at config-apply time (CI + control plane) and emit deterministic, actionable errors and automated migration suggestions for deprecated constructs.
acceptance_criteria: New validator runs as a staged CI job and fails fast on malformed routing configs
Validator enforces: canonical region identifiers, explicit tier precedence, model-variant compatibility, and required fallback definitions
Provide machine-readable warnings for deprecated fields and an automated mapper that suggests safe config transforms
End-to-end integration test that deploys a small routing config across two regions and demonstrates fallback to lower-tier model under capacity constraint
No regressions in existing policy coverage: existing test-suite must pass after enabling the validator in CI with a compatibility flag
tech_notes: Implement a layered validator: 1) syntactic DSL grammar (fast parse), 2) type checks & enum validation, 3) cross-field semantic checks and 4) cluster-aware compatibility (lookups against model catalog)
Use the new typed-ast produced by the parser to drive rule checks; keep the AST stable to avoid churn in downstream tools
Model catalog lookups will be read-only during validation: use a cached catalog snapshot in CI to prevent flakiness
Introduce a migration adaptor that can output 'safe transform' patches in YAML/JSON for user review
Preserve backwards compatibility: default to 'legacy-mode' off by flag. Gradually flip flag for internal repo configs and announce external breaking change
Performance target: validation pass should complete under 300ms for typical route manifests (~50 rules) in CI environment
migration_plan: Phase 1 (beta): Run validator in CI for all PRs and post results as a GitHub check. Validator runs in 'warn' mode so no blocking on external customers
Phase 2 (internal rollouts): Enable strict mode for internal infra repos; create automated PRs with suggested transforms for trivial deprecations
Phase 3 (customer rollout): Outreach to customers with invalid configs detected via telemetry; offer one-click migration via Console guided flow
Phase 4 (enforcement): After 8 weeks and customer notification, enable enforcement for new config uploads and control-plane changes
risks: False positives could block customer rollouts if strict mode is enabled prematurely
Catalog snapshot drift may cause spurious failures — requires versioned snapshots and clear caching TTL
Complex fallback chains (multi-step variant fallback) may be difficult to statically validate; runtime guards still required
test_plan: Unit tests for parser and each validation layer (grammar/type/semantic)
Property-based fuzzing for DSL inputs to ensure validator fails safely and never panics
Integration test harness that simulates capacity pressure and verifies fallback routing executes as validated
Regression suite to compare old vs. new validator outputs for historical configs stored in infra repo
rollout: Week 1: run validator in 'warn' mode for all internal repos and add GitHub check
Week 3: enable strict mode for infra and platform-owned configs
Week 6: provide console toggle for customers to preview migration suggestions
Week 10: enforce validation for control-plane config changes (after final communication)
implementation_notes: Language: Rust for the parser/validator module to align with runtime components and to maximize performance
Expose validator as a small standalone binary + WASM build for in-browser Console preview
Design validator API to return structured 'Diagnostic' list: code, message, severity, remediation_hint, suggested_patch (as text)
Store suggested_patch as plain text in CI artifacts for human review before auto-apply
